reported_numbers.acceleration: limited-memory Broyden in the perpendicular hyperplane

rubric.text: Represents the path as an ordered set of images between the two states and evolves all of them together.
Moves each image by only the component of the force perpendicular to the path, explicitly projecting out the component along the tangent, which is what stops the images from sliding into the minima.
Computes the tangent from the path itself at each step.
Redistributes the images along the curve to an even spacing (equal arc length) after the motion step, instead of holding them apart with spring forces between neighbours.
Holds the two endpoints fixed at the given stable states.
Reads the barrier as the highest energy along the converged path.
